frequency_question: How often do federal regulatory principals possessing the statutory will and capability successfully execute the revocation of a long-standing national accrediting body within a designated multi-year administrative window?
membership_rule: Includes any executive branch department action formally stripping recognition from a primary national professional or educational accreditor. Excludes voluntary relinquishments or standard periodic renewals without revocation intent.

cases.name: US Department of Education vs. American Bar Association (historical threat/review context)
US Department of Education vs. Accrediting Council for Independent Colleges and Schools (ACICS)
US Department of Education vs. ACICS (second termination after reinstatement)

provenance_note: 3 cases named, 4 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.3x)
coverage_note: 4 major contested federal recognition termination proceedings identified over three decades; 2 resulted in final revocation.
known_gaps: Excludes minor institutional or programmatic accreditors where federal withdrawal of recognition did not involve high-salience legal/political battles.
skeleton: Active administrative challenges to major institutional accreditors by the federal education principal resulting in terminal decertification events over a 30-year span.
multiplier: 2 hits out of roughly 4 major contested review proceedings where revocation was actively sought by the principal = 50%
validity_reason: Administrative enforcement priorities and statutory frameworks governing federal recognition of accreditors remain stable across multi-year executive cycles.
